ci.scope: Full supported-version matrix (10 smoke rows: torch 2.1 to 2.13, py3.10 to 3.13), lint, typing, packaging, nightly fast/mid/heavy/serial tiers and previews, weekly slow/rare and mutation margins, latest-torch canary, the opt-in 100k+ node graph suite, and the release dry run. Reuse an unchanged passing result; never rerun locally instead.
ci.status: Integrated 2026-10-03: every workflow runs on push to ci/** and on workflow_dispatch (release.yml on main only), and every job carries timeout-minutes within the budgets above (nightly jobs 30 to 120, weekly extended-tests 330).

notes: Inner loop: test-tier inner --changed PATH or --test tests/file.py::test_name. The map is deliberately partial; unmapped changes require reviewed targets and never fall back to the whole suite.

Commit gate: pytest tests/ -m smoke -n 4 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 (pytest-xdist ships in the dev extra). Smoke is ~1,476 coverage-chosen tests, about 1.5 to 2 minutes on 4 cores; tests/test_marker_lint.py caps it at 1,500, so a new smoke test needs a matching demotion.

Markers: smoke < 5 s each, heavy 5 to 20 s, slow > 20 s, serial runs without xdist (CI runs it in a separate step), rare is excluded by default, big_memory marks slow tests that exceed a 16 GB GitHub runner. The duration tripwire is load-calibrated by a measured slowdown probe (clamped 1x to 4x) and prints its factors in the terminal summary.

Pre_merge is the phase-boundary tier: 8 single-process shards over 'not rare and not slow' with one seed and one revision. The tier measured ~21-26 minutes at -n 4 on a 4-core worker (~90 core-minutes), so ~12 minutes of tests per shard plus uv setup and collection, inside the 25-minute slice. Each shard is one process, so serial tests run safely. Timeout or a refused shard is incomplete validation, never a pass.

Weekly GitHub slow tier runs one pytest process per file (scripts/run_pytest_per_file_sharded.py), batching large files and running tests/test_real_world_models.py one test per process; big_memory tests are excluded there.

big_memory tests run in the project-registry scheduled suite weekly-big-memory (Sat 06:30 UTC on a large-memory fleet worker, 24 GiB, 2 h timeout), declared in ~/desk/provision/project-registry.json, not here.
tests/known_failures.py holds the strict-xfail ledger of known real-model failures (round 2); a fixed model turns its strict xfail red, so the ledger only shrinks.
Linux workers need uv, Python 3.11 and Graphviz. Oracle goldens exist per environment; off-canonical environments fail locally and skip only when CI is set.
